description: Defines how A.R.I.A. determines whether a diagnosis, corrective action, configuration, installation, technical state, or case resolution has been sufficiently validated before accepting the result or allowing the case to contribute authoritative learning.

core_principle.statement: A corrective action is not a validated resolution. ARIA shall define expected post-action outcomes before validation, compare observed results against those expectations, distinguish operational recovery from causal proof, and preserve residual uncertainty.
rules: Validation criteria should be defined before evaluating the result whenever practical.
A successful action does not automatically prove the suspected root cause.
The disappearance of a symptom does not automatically prove complete resolution.
Validation shall use evidence appropriate to the technical condition being validated.
Validation strength shall reflect evidence quality, independence, applicability, duration, and completeness.
Failed validation shall become new evidence and return the case to active reasoning.
Validation shall never rewrite unsuccessful diagnostic history.
Learning eligibility shall depend on what was actually validated.

validation_types.name: DIRECT_REMEASUREMENT
validation_types.description: Repeat an applicable measurement after an intervention and compare the result against expected state.

validation_types.name: BEFORE_AFTER_COMPARISON
validation_types.description: Compare validated technical state before and after a controlled change.

validation_types.name: CONFIGURATION_VERIFICATION
validation_types.description: Verify that applicable configuration values match intended technical requirements.

validation_types.name: PHYSICAL_VERIFICATION
validation_types.description: Verify physical installation, routing, connection, orientation, component, or mechanical state.

validation_types.name: FUNCTIONAL_TEST
validation_types.description: Verify that the affected system performs its required function.

validation_types.name: PERFORMANCE_TEST
validation_types.description: Verify performance against engineering, manufacturer, customer, or project criteria.

validation_types.name: CROSS_ENDPOINT_VALIDATION
validation_types.description: Verify corresponding technical state from both ends of a path or system.

validation_types.name: INDEPENDENT_MEASUREMENT
validation_types.description: Validate a condition using an independent source or measurement method.

validation_types.name: CONTROLLED_INTERVENTION
validation_types.description: Change one sufficiently isolated variable and evaluate whether the predicted result occurs.

validation_types.name: REVERSAL_TEST
validation_types.description: Where safe and justified, reverse a controlled change to test whether the original condition returns.

validation_types.name: MONITORED_STABILITY
validation_types.description: Observe the technical state over a defined period to establish durability.

validation_types.name: ACCEPTANCE_VALIDATION
validation_types.description: Compare final state against applicable acceptance requirements.

rules: ARIA should know what result would constitute success before observing the result.
Thresholds shall be quantitative when technically appropriate.
Qualitative criteria shall be explicit when quantitative criteria are unavailable.
Validation plans shall reflect applicable manufacturer, engineering, customer, project, and safety requirements.
Required outcomes must normally be satisfied for full validation.
Supporting outcomes may increase confidence without being independently sufficient.
Unexpected improvement shall still be investigated when it contradicts the predicted mechanism.
Validation confidence shall preserve component factors.
A single weak validation method shall not receive artificial confidence from repeated copies of the same evidence.
Validation confidence may increase through independent corroboration.
Confidence shall remain bounded by material unresolved contradictions.

symptom_validation.description: Determines whether the originally reported or observed symptom remains present.
rules: The original symptom shall be explicitly reevaluated after corrective action.
If multiple symptoms existed, each material symptom shall be evaluated.
Symptom disappearance may establish operational improvement without proving exact root cause.

root_cause_validation.description: Determines whether evidence sufficiently establishes the causal mechanism responsible for the failure.
rules: Root-cause validation requires stronger evidence than symptom resolution.
Multiple simultaneous interventions shall reduce causal confidence.
Historical probability may support but shall not independently validate root cause.
A successful replacement may implicate the replaced subsystem without proving the exact failed mechanism.

corrective_action_validation.description: Determines whether a corrective action produced the intended technical effect.
required_questions: Was the intended action actually completed?
Did the targeted technical state change?
rules: Action completion and action effectiveness shall be separately recorded.
An ineffective corrective action is diagnostically useful evidence.
A partially effective correction may indicate multiple simultaneous failure mechanisms.
Configured values shall be compared against the applicable intended state.
Configuration presence does not prove configuration effectiveness.
Dependencies between configuration parameters shall be evaluated where applicable.
Both endpoints shall be considered when configuration relationships span the path.
Visual confirmation may validate visible installation state.
Hidden mating, internal electrical state, or RF performance may require additional evidence.
Component identity and port identity shall be confirmed when technically material.
Physical validation shall preserve endpoint and RF-chain context.

cross_endpoint_validation.description: Microwave systems frequently require validation across both endpoints rather than evaluating one radio in isolation.
rules: ARIA shall identify when a technical condition depends on both endpoints.
Near-end improvement shall not automatically establish far-end correctness.
Transmit and receive relationships shall preserve directionality.
Main and Diversity paths shall remain distinguishable.
Cross-endpoint disagreement shall trigger investigation rather than averaging.
The selected baseline shall be technically applicable.
A historical baseline shall not automatically remain valid after topology or configuration changes.
Engineered expectation and observed historical performance shall remain distinguishable.

tolerance_handling.description: Validation shall account for technically meaningful tolerances rather than requiring exact equality.
rules: Tolerance shall be derived from applicable engineering, manufacturer, customer, measurement, or statistical criteria.
Measurement uncertainty shall be considered.
A value barely inside a threshold may justify monitoring when other evidence remains concerning.
ARIA shall not invent numerical tolerances when no justified threshold exists.
Some corrections may be validated immediately.
Intermittent or environmentally dependent failures may require monitoring.
A case may be operationally restored while remaining in monitoring state.
Monitoring duration shall reflect the failure mechanism and recurrence risk rather than arbitrary time.

regression_check.description: Validation shall determine whether corrective work introduced new technical problems.

multi_change_caution.description: When multiple variables change before validation, ARIA shall reduce confidence in causal attribution.

example.valid_conclusion: The intervention set restored Diversity performance.
example.invalid_conclusion: The flex twist was definitely defective.

rules: Failed validation shall not restart the case.
The failed corrective action shall remain part of the diagnostic history.
The failure itself may strongly weaken the causal hypothesis that justified the action.
Unexpected outcomes may generate new hypotheses.

examples: RSL normalized but BER remains abnormal.
Main path passes while Diversity remains degraded.
Service restored but intermittent alarms continue.
Configuration corrected but engineered performance is not achieved.
rules: Partial success shall not be collapsed into PASS.
Remaining abnormal conditions shall return to active reasoning.
Successfully validated portions shall remain preserved and need not be unnecessarily retested.

resolution_gate.description: Controls whether a case may transition into a resolved state.
rules: A case may be operationally resolved without being causally resolved.
ARIA shall state the actual resolution level.
Cases with unresolved material service impact shall not be represented as fully resolved.
Resolution shall be controlled by deterministic state-transition rules.

learning_gate.description: Determines what aspects of a case may teach the Learning Engine.
rules: Validated symptom resolution alone does not authorize full causal learning.
Root-cause learning requires sufficient causal validation.
Route learning may remain valid when root cause is unresolved.
Learning restrictions shall be attached to the completed case.

predicted_outcome.diversity_rsl: Move materially toward expected engineered level

example.interpretation: The predicted technical response occurred after a targeted correction, strongly supporting the routing-error diagnosis and allowing appropriately weighted causal learning.

counterexample.learning_result: Do not teach ARIA that the flex twist was definitively defective. The intervention set may contribute route and subsystem-level experience.

engine_interfaces.case_state_engine: Controls validation lifecycle and resolution state.
engine_interfaces.evidence_engine: Provides validation evidence and evidence quality.
engine_interfaces.context_engine: Determines applicable technical context and criteria.
engine_interfaces.knowledge_graph: Provides expected states, relationships, procedures, and requirements.
engine_interfaces.probability_engine: Receives probability effects from validation outcomes.
engine_interfaces.routing_engine: Receives failed or partial validation as new routing state.
engine_interfaces.memory_engine: Provides applicable baselines and historical comparison.
engine_interfaces.learning_engine: Receives validation strength and learning restrictions.

semantic_rules.rule: A corrective action is not a validated resolution.
ARIA shall define expected outcomes before evaluating corrective success whenever practical.
Symptom resolution and root-cause validation are separate conclusions.
Multiple simultaneous changes shall reduce exact causal attribution confidence.
Validation shall use evidence appropriate to the condition being tested.
Validation evidence shall preserve provenance.
Repeated copies of the same validation evidence shall not create independent corroboration.
Failed validation is diagnostic evidence, not wasted work.
Failed validation shall trigger rerouting from the current state rather than restart.
Partial validation shall preserve successful findings while continuing diagnosis of unresolved conditions.
Applicable tolerance and measurement uncertainty shall be considered when evaluating technical success.
ARIA shall not invent acceptance criteria or technical tolerances.
Cross-endpoint systems shall be validated across all technically necessary endpoints.
Immediate improvement may require continued monitoring when recurrence risk remains material.
A case shall record the level of resolution actually achieved rather than force every closure into complete causal certainty.
Learning authorization shall reflect validation strength.
The language model may propose validation criteria, but authoritative validation state shall be controlled by structured ARIA services.
Successful validation shall not erase contradictory evidence; material contradictions must be reconciled or preserved.
Validation shall check for unintended regression where technically applicable.
ARIA shall prefer validated technical resolution over conversational agreement that the problem appears fixed.
